name: cache
description: Caching for services: immutable LRU and TTL caches with stats, a shared SQLite cache with single-flight, and HTTP caching (ETags, conditional requests, Cache-Control)

api.name: Config
api.sig: pub type Config = {capacity: Int where _ >= 1, max_cost: Int where _ >= 0, ttl_ms: Int where _ >= 0, refresh_on_get: Bool} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
How a cache is bounded: at most `capacity` entries and, when `max_cost` is above 0, a total cost
of at most `max_cost` (each entry's cost is given when it is put; 1 by default). `ttl_ms` above 0
is the default time to live; `refresh_on_get` restarts an entry's time to live when it is read
(expire after access instead of after write).

api.name: Stats
api.sig: pub type Stats = {hits: Int, misses: Int, puts: Int, evictions: Int, expirations: Int} derive Eq, Show, Json
api.doc:
Counters of what a cache did: reads that found a live entry and reads that didn't, writes,
entries evicted for room, and entries dropped because they had expired.

api.name: Entry
api.sig: pub type Entry[V] = {value: V, tick: Int, expires_ms: Opt[Int], ttl_ms: Int, cost: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
One cached value with its recency tick, its expiry time (none for never), its time to live and
its cost.

api.name: Cache
api.sig: pub type Cache[K, V] = {config: Config, entries: Map[K, Entry[V]], order: Set[(Int, K)], expiry: Set[(Int, Int, K)], tick: Int, cost: Int, stats: Stats} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
An immutable LRU cache from K to V. Every operation returns the new cache; reads that change
recency or statistics return it too. Operations are O(log n). The least recently used live
entry is evicted first, after any expired ones.

api.name: config
api.sig: fn config(capacity: Int where _ >= 1) -> Config
api.doc: A configuration bounded by `capacity` entries only.

api.name: new
api.sig: fn new[K, V](cfg: Config) -> Cache[K, V]
api.doc: An empty cache with configuration `cfg`.

api.name: lru
api.sig: fn lru[K, V](capacity: Int where _ >= 1) -> Cache[K, V]
api.doc: An empty LRU cache of at most `capacity` entries.

api.name: ttl_lru
api.sig: fn ttl_lru[K, V](capacity: Int where _ >= 1, ttl_ms: Int where _ >= 1) -> Cache[K, V]
api.doc: An empty LRU cache of at most `capacity` entries that each live `ttl_ms` after they are written.

api.name: size
api.sig: fn size[K, V](c: Cache[K, V]) -> Int
api.doc: The number of entries, live or expired but not yet dropped.

api.name: total_cost
api.sig: fn total_cost[K, V](c: Cache[K, V]) -> Int
api.doc: The total cost of the entries.

api.name: hit_rate
api.sig: fn hit_rate(s: Stats) -> F64
api.doc: The fraction of reads that hit, 0.0 before any read.

api.name: peek
api.sig: fn peek[K, V](c: Cache[K, V], k: K, now_ms: Int) -> Opt[V]
api.doc: The value for `k` if it is there and live, without touching recency or statistics.

api.name: has
api.sig: fn has[K, V](c: Cache[K, V], k: K, now_ms: Int) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `k` has a live entry.

api.name: get
api.sig: fn get[K, V](c: Cache[K, V], k: K, now_ms: Int) -> (Opt[V], Cache[K, V])
api.doc:
Reads `k`: the value of a live entry, which becomes the most recently used (and with
`refresh_on_get` gets a new expiry), counted as a hit; otherwise none, counted as a miss, and
an expired entry is dropped.

api.name: touch
api.sig: fn touch[K, V](c: Cache[K, V], k: K, now_ms: Int) -> Cache[K, V]
api.doc:
Marks `k` as just used and restarts its time to live, without reading it (and without counting
a hit). Missing or expired keys are left alone.

api.name: put
api.sig: fn put[K, V](c: Cache[K, V], k: K, v: V, now_ms: Int) -> Cache[K, V]
api.doc: Writes `k` with the default time to live and a cost of 1, evicting what must go.

api.name: put_ttl
api.sig: fn put_ttl[K, V](c: Cache[K, V], k: K, v: V, now_ms: Int, ttl_ms: Int where _ >= 1) -> Cache[K, V]
api.doc: Writes `k` to live `ttl_ms` milliseconds.

api.name: insert
api.sig: fn insert[K, V](c: Cache[K, V], k: K, v: V, now_ms: Int, ttl_ms: Opt[Int], cost: Int where _ >= 0) -> (Cache[K, V], List[(K, V)])
api.doc:
Writes `k` with a time to live (none: it never expires, whatever the default) and a cost, and
returns the entries that left to make room or because they had expired, so the caller can
release them. An entry that costs more than `max_cost` is not stored, and an older entry for `k`
is removed.

api.name: purge_expired
api.sig: fn purge_expired[K, V](c: Cache[K, V], now_ms: Int) -> (Cache[K, V], List[(K, V)])
api.doc: Drops every entry that has expired by `now_ms`; returns the cache and the dropped entries.

api.name: remove
api.sig: fn remove[K, V](c: Cache[K, V], k: K) -> Cache[K, V]
api.doc: Removes `k` (not counted as an eviction).

api.name: take
api.sig: fn take[K, V](c: Cache[K, V], k: K, now_ms: Int) -> (Opt[V], Cache[K, V])
api.doc: Removes `k` and returns its value if it was live.

api.name: clear
api.sig: fn clear[K, V](c: Cache[K, V]) -> Cache[K, V]
api.doc: Removes every entry, keeping the configuration and the statistics.

api.name: resize
api.sig: fn resize[K, V](c: Cache[K, V], capacity: Int where _ >= 1, max_cost: Int where _ >= 0) -> (Cache[K, V], List[(K, V)])
api.doc:
Changes the bounds, evicting least recently used entries until the cache fits; returns the
evicted entries too.

api.name: keys
api.sig: fn keys[K, V](c: Cache[K, V]) -> List[K]
api.doc: The keys, most recently used first (expired ones not yet dropped included).

api.name: items
api.sig: fn items[K, V](c: Cache[K, V], now_ms: Int) -> List[(K, V)]
api.doc: The live entries at `now_ms`, most recently used first.

api.name: lru_key
api.sig: fn lru_key[K, V](c: Cache[K, V]) -> Opt[K]
api.doc: The key that would be evicted next (the least recently used).

api.name: mru_key
api.sig: fn mru_key[K, V](c: Cache[K, V]) -> Opt[K]
api.doc: The most recently used key.

api.name: ttl_left
api.sig: fn ttl_left[K, V](c: Cache[K, V], k: K, now_ms: Int) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc: The milliseconds `k` has left to live: none if it is missing, expired or never expires.

api.name: get_or_compute
api.sig: fn get_or_compute[K, V, e](c: Cache[K, V], k: K, now_ms: Int, f: K -> V ! e) -> (V, Cache[K, V]) ! e
api.doc: The value for `k`, computed by `f` and stored when it is missing or expired.

api.name: stats
api.sig: fn stats[K, V](c: Cache[K, V]) -> Stats
api.doc: The statistics.

api.name: Shared
api.sig: pub type Shared = {db: Db, table: Str, capacity: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A cache of text values in a SQLite table, shared by the concurrent handlers of a server (the
Db is shared; a ":memory:" database is one connection) and by processes that open the same
file. Every operation is a transaction, so reads and writes from anywhere stay consistent. It
keeps at most `capacity` entries, evicting expired ones first and then the least recently used
(each read records its use, so a read is a small write). Values are `Str`: a library can't decode
JSON into a type parameter, so store `json.encode(x)` and decode on the way out (`shared_get_as` and
`shared_put_as` do it with a decoder you pass). Statistics are kept in the database too.

api.name: Flight
api.sig: pub type Flight = {lease_ms: Int where _ >= 1, wait_ms: Int where _ >= 0, poll_ms: Int where _ >= 1} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
How `fetch` waits for another caller computing the same key: the lease a computer holds (when
it crashes or raises, others take over after it), how long a waiter waits before computing the
value itself, and how often it looks.

api.name: valid_table_name
api.sig: fn valid_table_name(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether `s` can name the cache's tables: a letter or underscore, then letters, digits and
underscores, at most 50 characters (the tables get suffixes).

api.name: shared
api.sig: fn shared(c: Db, table: Str where valid_table_name(_), capacity: Int where _ >= 1) -> Shared ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
Opens the cache `table` in `c` with room for `capacity` entries, creating its tables when
missing (`table`, `table_meta` for the statistics and `table_leases` for single-flight).

api.name: flight
api.sig: fn flight() -> Flight
api.doc: The default single-flight settings: 30 s leases, waiters wait up to 30 s, polling every 10 ms.

api.name: shared_get
api.sig: fn shared_get(s: Shared, key: Str, now_ms: Int) -> Opt[Str] ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
Reads `key`: its value when it is there and live (now the most recently used), counted as a
hit; otherwise none, counted as a miss (an expired entry is deleted).

api.name: shared_peek
api.sig: fn shared_peek(s: Shared, key: Str, now_ms: Int) -> Opt[Str] ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: The value of `key` if it is live, reading only: no recency, no statistics.

api.name: shared_put
api.sig: fn shared_put(s: Shared, key: Str, value: Str, now_ms: Int, ttl_ms: Int where _ >= 0) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
Writes `key` to live `ttl_ms` milliseconds (0: until evicted); returns how many entries left to
make room (expired ones first, then the least recently used).

api.name: shared_delete
api.sig: fn shared_delete(s: Shared, key: Str) -> Bool ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Deletes `key`: whether it was there.

api.name: shared_clear
api.sig: fn shared_clear(s: Shared) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Deletes every entry; returns how many there were. Statistics are kept.

api.name: shared_purge
api.sig: fn shared_purge(s: Shared, now_ms: Int) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Deletes the entries that have expired by `now_ms`; returns how many.

api.name: shared_count
api.sig: fn shared_count(s: Shared) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: The number of entries, live or expired but not yet deleted.

api.name: shared_stats
api.sig: fn shared_stats(s: Shared) -> Stats ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: The statistics of the shared cache, summed over every process that uses it.

api.name: shared_get_as
api.sig: fn shared_get_as[T](s: Shared, key: Str, now_ms: Int, decode: Str -> Opt[T]) -> Opt[T] ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
Reads `key` and decodes it with `decode` (such as `x => json.decode[User](x).map(some).or(none)`);
a value that doesn't decode counts as missing.

api.name: shared_put_as
api.sig: fn shared_put_as[T: Json](s: Shared, key: Str, value: T, now_ms: Int, ttl_ms: Int where _ >= 0) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Writes `value` as its JSON.

api.name: shared_computing
api.sig: fn shared_computing(s: Shared, key: Str, now_ms: Int) -> Bool ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Whether someone holds a live lease on `key`, computing it.

api.name: fetch
api.sig: fn fetch[e](s: Shared, key: Str, ttl_ms: Int, f: Flight, compute: () -> Str ! e) -> Str ! db, fail[DbErr], time, rand, div, e
api.doc:
The value of `key`, computed by `compute` (and stored for `ttl_ms`, 0 or less for no expiry) when it is
missing, with single-flight: of the callers that miss at the same time, in this process or any
other sharing the database, one takes a lease and computes while the others wait and get its
result. A waiter that waits longer than `f.wait_ms` computes the value itself. When a computer
crashes or `compute` raises, its lease runs out after `f.lease_ms` and the next caller takes over.

api.name: fetch_as
api.sig: fn fetch_as[T: Json, e](s: Shared, key: Str, ttl_ms: Int, f: Flight, compute: () -> T ! e, decode: Str -> Opt[T]) -> T ! db, fail[DbErr], time, rand, div, e
api.doc:
`fetch` for a JSON-encodable type: computes a `T`, stores its JSON, and decodes a cached value
with `decode`; a cached value that doesn't decode is computed again.

api.name: Etag
api.sig: pub type Etag = {weak: Bool, tag: Str} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: An entity tag (RFC 9110 8.8.3): its opaque text, without quotes, and whether it is weak.

api.name: etag_text_ok
api.sig: fn etag_text_ok(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether `s` can be the text of an entity tag: etagc characters only (no spaces, quotes or
control characters).

api.name: strong_etag
api.sig: fn strong_etag(tag: Str where etag_text_ok(_)) -> Etag
api.doc: A strong entity tag with text `tag`.

api.name: weak_etag
api.sig: fn weak_etag(tag: Str where etag_text_ok(_)) -> Etag
api.doc: A weak entity tag with text `tag`.

api.name: etag_str
api.sig: fn etag_str(e: Etag) -> Str
api.doc: The field value of an entity tag: `"tag"` or `W/"tag"`.

api.name: parse_etag
api.sig: fn parse_etag(s: Str) -> Opt[Etag]
api.doc: Parses one entity tag, `"..."` or `W/"..."`.

api.name: etag_for
api.sig: fn etag_for(body: Str) -> Etag
api.doc:
A strong entity tag for a body: 128 bits of its SHA-256 in base64url, so the same body always
has the same tag. Use it when the bytes sent are the body itself.

api.name: weak_etag_for
api.sig: fn weak_etag_for(body: Str) -> Etag
api.doc:
A weak entity tag for a body, for responses the server may compress or otherwise transform
(the `gzip` server field), whose bytes then differ from the body.

api.name: strong_match
api.sig: fn strong_match(a: Etag, b: Etag) -> Bool
api.doc: Strong comparison (RFC 9110 8.8.3.2): both strong and the same text.

api.name: weak_match
api.sig: fn weak_match(a: Etag, b: Etag) -> Bool
api.doc: Weak comparison: the same text, whatever the weakness.

api.name: Condition
api.sig: pub type Condition = AnyTag | Tags{tags: List[Etag]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: The value of an If-Match or If-None-Match field: `*` or a list of entity tags.

api.name: parse_condition
api.sig: fn parse_condition(s: Str) -> Opt[Condition]
api.doc:
Parses an If-Match or If-None-Match value; none when it is malformed (a `*` mixed with tags,
or an invalid tag) or empty.

api.name: format_http_date
api.sig: fn format_http_date(t: Time) -> Str
api.doc:
An HTTP date in the preferred IMF-fixdate form, `Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT` (RFC 9110 5.6.7).
Milliseconds are dropped.

api.name: parse_http_date
api.sig: fn parse_http_date(s: Str, now: Time) -> Opt[Time]
api.doc:
Parses an HTTP date in any of the three forms recipients must accept: IMF-fixdate, the obsolete
RFC 850 form (a two-digit year, read relative to `now`) and asctime. Names are case-sensitive and
the time zone must be GMT, as the RFC says; none for anything else.

api.name: Validators
api.sig: pub type Validators = {etag: Opt[Etag], last_modified: Opt[Time]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
What the server knows about the current representation: its entity tag and its modification
time, either of which may be missing.

api.name: Outcome
api.sig: pub type Outcome = Proceed | NotModified | PreconditionFailed derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
The result of evaluating a request's preconditions: go on, answer 304 Not Modified, or answer
412 Precondition Failed.

api.name: evaluate
api.sig: fn evaluate(req: Request, v: Validators, exists: Bool, now: Time) -> Outcome
api.doc:
Evaluates the preconditions of `req` against the current representation (`exists` is whether
there is one) in the order of RFC 9110 13.2.2: If-Match (strong comparison; a malformed value
fails), else If-Unmodified-Since; then If-None-Match (weak comparison: 304 for GET and HEAD,
412 otherwise), else If-Modified-Since for GET and HEAD. Dates compare at whole seconds;
malformed or repeated dates, and If-Modified-Since dates after `now`, are ignored. Call it
before changing anything for PUT, PATCH and DELETE.

api.name: validators_of
api.sig: fn validators_of(r: Response, now: Time) -> Validators
api.doc: The validators a response carries: its ETag and Last-Modified fields.

api.name: not_modified
api.sig: fn not_modified(r: Response) -> Response
api.doc:
The 304 Not Modified answer for a 200 response (RFC 9110 15.4.5): no body and no
representation metadata (Content-*), keeping ETag, Cache-Control, Expires, Vary, Date,
Content-Location and the other fields; Last-Modified only when there is no ETag.

api.name: precondition_failed
api.sig: fn precondition_failed(v: Validators) -> Response
api.doc: The 412 Precondition Failed answer, with the current entity tag when there is one.

api.name: conditional
api.sig: fn conditional(req: Request, r: Response, now: Time) -> Response
api.doc:
Applies conditional GET to a response already made: for a GET or HEAD answered 200, the
request's preconditions are evaluated against the response's own ETag and Last-Modified, giving
304 or 412 where they say so. Other requests and statuses pass unchanged.

api.name: set_header
api.sig: fn set_header(r: Response, name: Str, value: Str) -> Response
api.doc: Sets field `name` (case-insensitively replacing any) on a response.

api.name: with_etag
api.sig: fn with_etag(r: Response, weak: Bool) -> Response
api.doc: Adds an ETag computed from the body (weak with `weak`) to a 200 response that has none.

api.name: conditional_get
api.sig: fn conditional_get[e](weak: Bool, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e, time
api.doc:
Wraps a handler with conditional GET: 200 answers to GET and HEAD get an ETag from their body
(weak with `weak`, which suits the server's `gzip` field) unless they have one, and the
request's If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since, If-Match and If-Unmodified-Since are applied to them.
The handler still runs (this saves bandwidth, not work). Build it inside the handler lambda.

api.name: CacheControl
api.sig: pub type CacheControl = {max_age: Opt[Int], s_maxage: Opt[Int], no_cache: Bool, no_cache_fields: List[Str], no_store: Bool, private: Bool, private_fields: List[Str], public: Bool, must_revalidate: Bool, proxy_revalidate: Bool, must_understand: Bool, no_transform: Bool, immutable: Bool, stale_while_revalidate: Opt[Int], stale_if_error: Opt[Int], max_stale: Opt[Int], min_fresh: Opt[Int], only_if_cached: Bool, extensions: List[(Str, Str)]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
The directives of a Cache-Control field (RFC 9111 5.2), for responses and requests. Durations
are in seconds; `max_stale` without a value is 2147483648. Unknown directives are kept in
`extensions` with their values ("" for none).

api.name: cache_control
api.sig: fn cache_control() -> CacheControl
api.doc: No directives.

api.name: no_store
api.sig: fn no_store() -> CacheControl
api.doc: `no-store`: for anything personal or secret.

api.name: revalidate
api.sig: fn revalidate() -> CacheControl
api.doc: `no-cache`: caches may store it but must revalidate every time (pair it with an ETag).

api.name: public_for
api.sig: fn public_for(secs: Int where _ >= 0) -> CacheControl
api.doc: `public, max-age=secs`.

api.name: private_for
api.sig: fn private_for(secs: Int where _ >= 0) -> CacheControl
api.doc: `private, max-age=secs`: only the user's own browser may keep it.

api.name: immutable_for
api.sig: fn immutable_for(secs: Int where _ >= 0) -> CacheControl
api.doc: `public, max-age=secs, immutable`: for assets whose URL changes with their content.

api.name: render_cache_control
api.sig: fn render_cache_control(cc: CacheControl) -> Str
api.doc: The field value of a Cache-Control, directives in a fixed order.

api.name: cache_control_header
api.sig: fn cache_control_header(cc: CacheControl) -> (Str, Str)
api.doc: The Cache-Control field for `cc`.

api.name: with_cache_control
api.sig: fn with_cache_control(r: Response, cc: CacheControl) -> Response
api.doc: Sets the Cache-Control field of a response, replacing any.

api.name: parse_delta
api.sig: fn parse_delta(s: Str) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc: A delta-seconds value: digits only, clamped to 2^31 as RFC 9111 1.2.2 says.

api.name: parse_cache_control
api.sig: fn parse_cache_control(s: Str) -> CacheControl
api.doc:
Parses a Cache-Control value: directive names are case-insensitive, values tokens or quoted
strings; of a repeated directive the first counts, and a malformed duration is ignored.

api.name: cache_control_of
api.sig: fn cache_control_of(r: Response) -> CacheControl
api.doc: The Cache-Control of a response, every field line together.

api.name: vary_of
api.sig: fn vary_of(r: Response) -> List[Str]
api.doc: The field names a response varies on (the Vary field lines together).

api.name: add_vary
api.sig: fn add_vary(r: Response, names: List[Str]) -> Response
api.doc:
Adds field names to the response's Vary, once each (case-insensitively), in one field line;
`*` absorbs everything.

api.name: freshness_lifetime
api.sig: fn freshness_lifetime(cc: CacheControl, shared: Bool, date: Opt[Time], expires: Opt[Str]) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
The freshness lifetime of a response in seconds (RFC 9111 4.2.1): s-maxage for a shared cache,
else max-age, else Expires minus Date (an invalid Expires means already stale); none when the
response says nothing (a heuristic lifetime is the cache's choice).

api.name: current_age
api.sig: fn current_age(age_value: Int where _ >= 0, date: Opt[Time], request_time: Time, response_time: Time, now: Time) -> Int
api.doc:
The current age of a stored response in seconds (RFC 9111 4.2.3), from its Age value, its Date,
when the request was sent, when the response arrived, and now.

api.name: is_fresh
api.sig: fn is_fresh(lifetime: Int, age: Int) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether a response of `lifetime` seconds and `age` seconds is still fresh.

api.name: age_header
api.sig: fn age_header(secs: Int where _ >= 0) -> (Str, Str)
api.doc: The Age field for `secs` seconds.
